---
title: "SEIR Model Simu"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load necessary packages
if(!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(deSolve,
               tidyverse,
               here)
```

```{r load-data}
# 1. LOAD OBSERVED DATA
observed_data <- read.csv("SIR.csv") 
head(observed_data) # Verifies column headers in console
```

```{r settings}
# 2. SET UP SEIR INITIAL CONDITIONS & PARAMETERS

# Total population N = 100 (S = 99, I = 1)
initial_state <- c(S = 99,   # Susceptible 
                   E = 0,    # Exposed (incubating)
                   I = 1,    # Infectious
                   R = 0)    # Recovered

# Parameters tuned to match a population scale of 100
parameters <- c(beta  = 0.014,  # Transmission rate
                sigma = 0.5,    # Incubation rate (2 days incubation period = 1/2 = 0.5)
                gamma = 0.2)    # Recovery rate (5 days infectious period = 1/5 = 0.2)

# Set the time span of 365 days starting at time = 0
time_span <- seq(0, 365, by = 1) 
```

```{r model-function}
# 3. DEFINE THE SEIR MODEL FUNCTION
seir_model <- function(time, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {

    # Rate of change equations
    dS <- -beta * S * I
    dE <-  beta * S * I - sigma * E
    dI <-  sigma * E - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    
    # Return the rates of change in the exact order of initial_state
    list(c(dS, dE, dI, dR))
  })
}
```

```{r solve}
# 4. SOLVE DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS
seir_out <- ode(
  y = initial_state,
  time = time_span,     
  func = seir_model,
  parms = parameters
)
```

```{r convert}
# 5. CONVERT OUTPUT TO A DATA FRAME
seir_out_df <- as.data.frame(seir_out)
```

```{r plot-dynamics}
# 6. VISUALIZE THE RESULTS SEIR
ggplot(seir_out_df, aes(x = time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = S, color = "Susceptible"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = E, color = "Exposed"), linewidth = 1) +      
  geom_line(aes(y = I, color = "Infected"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = R, color = "Recovered"), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "SEIR Model Dynamics Forecast",
       x = "Time (days)",
       y = "Population Count") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Susceptible" = "#2F5597", 
                                "Exposed"     = "#ED7D31",     
                                "Infected"    = "#C00000",
                                "Recovered"   = "#548235")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r plot-comparison}
# 7. VISUALIZE COMPARISON GRAPH
comparison_graph <- ggplot() +
  # Real world dataset tracking line (Sums Asymptomatic and Symptomatic)
  geom_line(data = observed_data,
            aes(x = X, y = Ia + Is, color = "Observed (Ia + Is)"),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = observed_data,
             aes(x = X, y = Ia + Is, color = "Observed (Ia + Is)"),
             size = 2) +
  # SEIR Model tracking line
  geom_line(data = seir_out_df,
            aes(x = time, y = I, color = "SEIR Model (I)"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed (Ia + Is)" = "black", "SEIR Model (I)" = "red")) +
  labs(title = "SEIR Model Fit vs. Observed Active Cases",
       x = "Time (Days)",
       y = "Active Infected Population",
       color = "Source") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Load graph
comparison_graph
```
